newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 15.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- RUSH TO SELL MAY HIT A&L PRICE

Hopes by investors that shares in Alliance & Leicester that new shareholders in the building society wanted to sell immediately. The move by the shareholders was the first indication of how investors may be reacting to the 22 billion stg demutualisation of A&L this year. The high level of members willing to share should ease the transfer of shares from retail to institutional hands.
-- FORMER CBS CHIEF IN JOB TALKS WITH C4 AND SONY

Former head of U.S. television network CBS, Howard Stringer, already named as being in talks with Sony to become its top U.S. director, has become a possible candidate for the chief executive opening at Channel 4. Stringer has also interviewed for the post of chief executive for the ITV Network Centre, but has ruled himself out as a candidate as he was not prepared to make a decision. Stringer's previous job was running Tele-TV, an interactive television merger between Bell TV and two other U.S. regional telephone companies.
-- FALL IN MANUFACTURING PRICES RAISES TORY INFLATION HOPES

After continued declines in manufacturers' input and output prices, the UK government is optimistic on reaching its 2.5 percent inflation rate. Areas that have seen especially low prices are imported goods and materials, and a British Retail Consortium survey indicated low prices in the retail sector as well. City analysts say the figures are an indication price inflation remains under control.
-- GEC ALSTHOM WINS 100 MILLION STG TRAINS DEAL

Anglo-French transport equipment group GEC Alsthom has announced a 100 million stg UK train deal with the Gatwick Express Service to supply and maintain eight-car trains. GEC won the deal over more than 20 international competitors and has committed itself to a tight schedule. It is the first successful bid by GEC Alsthom's Juniper project.
-- CAMELOT FALLS AGAIN IN BID TO STOP RIVAL LOTTERY

UK National Lottery operator Camelot has once again lost a High Court bid to prevent Ladbrokes, William Hill and Coral from running their own lottery, 49's. The court ruling stated a judicial review was not the proper fashion for Camelot to prosecute its rival companies for "unlawful lottery". The court also refused a Camelot appeal to the House of Lords, leading Camelot to consider the possibility of a private prosecuting.
-- PORTUGAL TELECOM PICKS BT AND MCI

Portugal Telecom has chosen Concert, the global alliance of BT and MCI of the United States, as its strategic partner. The decision will be followed by a number of corporate realignments set to reshape the European and U.S. telecoms industries. The Telefonica board is considering abandoning its relationship with the European Alliance Unisource, comprising Sweden, the Netherlands and Switzerland, for Concert. The official decision is expected later this week with the option of an alliance with AT&T, but observers believe there is an 80 percent chance Telefonica will opt for an alliance with BT and MCI.
-- PHILIP CROSBY BUYS BACK COMPANY HE FOUNDED

UK management consultancy Proudfoot is selling the quality management company Philip Crosby Associates for less than one million dollars, compared to the 87 million dollars they bought the company for in 1991, to company founder Philip Crosby. Philip Crosby Associates advises managers how to eradicate problems in processes and products. But the company has suffered a decline in profits from five million dollars, when Proudfoot bought the company, to a loss of 300,000 dollars after a $1.7 million reorganisation in 1996.
-- PEARL CONTRIBUTION LIFTS AMP TO ONE BILLION STG.

Financial services advisor Australian Mutual Provident said on Monday they were still interested in British acquisitions and announced that a one-off gain from subsidiary Pearl Group helped them to post a profit gain in 1996 after lower investment returns. After a rise in assets of 9.4 percent to 94.5 billion Australian dollars, due to management, net profits for AMP have increased from 1.9 billion to 2.1 billion Australian dollars in the year. This included a 479 million Australian dollar abnormal profit from UK Pearl group.
-- GUS PAYS 264 MILLION DOLLARS FOR DIRECT TECH

U.S. marketing information service group Direct Marketing Technology has been bought for 246.2 million dollars by Great Universal Stores on Monday in GUS's continuing corporate activity. Direct Tech's two founders along with other employees will receive a further 52.5 million dollars if they meet performance targets set for the next five years. They are also in receipt of 59 percent of the holdings valued at 131 million dollars. GUS deputy manager Eric Barnes stated the deal would complement the purchase of Experian, the US financial information services company, five months previous.
-- CAMAS MERGES WITH BARDON

The merger of building materials companies Camas and Bardon was announced on Monday, creating the UK's fifth largest aggregates producers. The combined market value on Monday night was 537.2 million stg following Bardons two-for-one share offer. Discussions of a merger in 1995 between the two companies were dissolved following disagreements concerned with price and management issues.
